title: LabelBench · Different jobs
question: What does the proxy do in LabelBench’s efficient path?
choices: Become the only final evaluated predictor.
Update the pretrained encoder every round.
explanation: The cheap proxy guides acquisition; the final model is fine-tuned end-to-end on the collected labels and remaining unlabeled inputs.

title: LabelBench · Frozen representation
question: Why can cached embeddings be reused during proxy training?
choices: They contain all future oracle labels.
The encoder weights remain fixed on this path.
They are outputs of the final changing encoder.
explanation: The fixed encoder gives a reusable feature representation. Final encoder fine-tuning cannot treat old cached features as current encoder outputs.

title: LabelBench · Acquisition arithmetic
question: For probabilities (0.45, 0.40, 0.15), what is the margin score?
explanation: The margin is the largest probability minus the second largest: 0.45 − 0.40 = 0.05. Margin sampling queries small gaps.

title: LabelBench · Truth versus guesses
question: The selected example was predicted as class 1; the oracle returns class 2. What enters L?
explanation: Acquisition happens before the hidden target is revealed. The oracle label supplies supervision and can contradict the proxy.

title: LabelBench · Two accuracy tasks
question: With 20 perfect oracle labels in a 100-item pool and 75% accuracy on the other 80, what is pool accuracy?
explanation: The completed pool has 20 correct oracle labels plus 60 correct model labels: 80/100. This is not held-out test accuracy.

title: LabelBench · State in the loop
question: What does the paper specify for proxy training at each acquisition round?
choices: Train the proxy from scratch on the updated partitions.
explanation: Section 4.1 trains the proxy from scratch. Collected annotations, partitions and cached features survive; proxy weights are not the stated carried state.

title: LabelBench · Uncertainty is not coverage
question: Why might uncertainty sampling select redundant examples?
choices: Every uncertain image belongs to a rare class.
Duplicates can have the same high uncertainty score.
It reads the hidden labels before ranking.
explanation: High uncertainty alone does not ensure distinct information. Diversity strategies use features or other geometry, with their own representation-dependent limitations.

title: LabelBench · Evidence boundaries
question: What does use of the WILDS datasets establish in this paper?
choices: The oracle cost includes real annotation time.
The reported evaluation uses in-domain test data.
explanation: The paper uses in-domain splits of iWildCam and fMoW and proposes distribution-shift evaluation as future work. Dataset provenance alone does not establish an OOD result.
